title: model-card template variables
description: Values for templates/model-card.md.j2 and templates/model-card.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from model-card.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

audit_log_path.title: Audit log path
audit_log_path.description: Where do those audit logs live - the path or URI an auditor opens without asking anyone?

base_model.title: Base model
base_model.description: Which base model was fine-tuned to produce this one? Write 'none' if it was trained from scratch; an unnamed base hides an inherited licence and an inherited bias.

dp_diff.title: Dp diff
dp_diff.description: What demographic-parity difference did the fairness audit measure?

dp_result.title: Dp result
dp_result.description: Did demographic parity clear its bar? A fail on a shipped model needs the reason written in Known limitations below.

dp_threshold.title: Dp threshold
dp_threshold.description: What demographic-parity difference was set as the pass bar, before the numbers were looked at?

eo_diff.title: Eo diff
eo_diff.description: What equalised-odds difference did the fairness audit measure?

eo_result.title: Eo result
eo_result.description: Did equalised odds clear its bar?

eo_threshold.title: Eo threshold
eo_threshold.description: What equalised-odds difference was set as the pass bar?

finetune_date.title: Finetune date
finetune_date.description: On what date was this fine-tune produced, as YYYY-MM-DD? Not the deployment date - the date the weights stopped changing.

intended_use_primary.title: Intended use primary
intended_use_primary.description: What is this model for? One sentence describing the use it was evaluated on; anything outside it is out of scope by construction.

intended_use_secondary.title: Intended use secondary
intended_use_secondary.description: What second use has been evaluated and is also supported? Write 'none' rather than leaving the row for a reader to interpret.

limit_1.title: Limit 1
limit_1.description: What is the first known limitation - a case where this model is reliably worse than a reader would expect? Say it before a customer finds it.

limit_2.title: Limit 2
limit_2.description: What is the second known limitation?

metric_1_ci.title: Metric 1 ci
metric_1_ci.description: What is the confidence interval around that first value? A point estimate with no interval cannot be compared with the next release.

metric_1_name.title: Metric 1 name
metric_1_name.description: Which evaluation metric is reported first, named precisely enough that someone else could compute the same number?

metric_1_value.title: Metric 1 value
metric_1_value.description: What value did that first metric take on the evaluation set?

metric_2_ci.title: Metric 2 ci
metric_2_ci.description: What is the confidence interval around that second value?

metric_2_name.title: Metric 2 name
metric_2_name.description: Which evaluation metric is reported second?

metric_2_value.title: Metric 2 value
metric_2_value.description: What value did that second metric take?

model_version.title: Model version
model_version.description: Which exact model version does this card describe? A card whose version cannot be matched to a deployed artefact attests to nothing.

out_of_scope_1.title: Out of scope 1
out_of_scope_1.description: What is the first use this model must not be put to? Pick the one a reasonable person would otherwise assume was fine.

out_of_scope_2.title: Out of scope 2
out_of_scope_2.description: What is the second use this model must not be put to?

oversight_policy.title: Oversight policy
oversight_policy.description: Where is the human-oversight policy written down - the document or path that says which outputs a human must see before they take effect?

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Which provider supplies this model - the account you are billed by and would file a ticket with?

retention_years.title: Retention years
retention_years.description: For how many years are this model's audit logs retained? Under the AI Act the floor is set by your risk class, not by your storage bill.

reviewers.title: Reviewers
reviewers.description: Who performs that oversight? Named humans or a named rota, never 'the team' - the EU AI Act obligation attaches to people.

sla.title: Sla
sla.description: How fast must a human be able to reverse an output of this model, from the moment it is challenged? State the time, not 'promptly'.

system_name.description: Which named system does this model serve - the one a regulator could find in your service catalogue? The card is filed against the system, not the weights.

training_dataset_summary.title: Training dataset summary
training_dataset_summary.description: What was this model trained on, in enough detail that a reader can judge who is under-represented? Sources, licences and rough proportions, not a dataset name alone.

training_window_end.title: Training window end
training_window_end.description: What is the latest date the training data covers, as YYYY-MM-DD? Everything after it is outside the model's knowledge whatever it claims.

training_window_start.title: Training window start
training_window_start.description: What is the earliest date the training data covers, as YYYY-MM-DD? This is half of what tells a reader which world the model still believes in.
